title: Optimize a List with trackBy
description: Add trackBy to a large list and observe performance improvement.
problemStatement:
Given a component that renders a large list of items (500+), implement `trackBy` to improve re‑render performance.

**Requirements:**
1. Create a component with an array of objects (e.g., `{ id: number, text: string }`).
2. Render them with `*ngFor`.
3. Add a button that re‑creates the entire array with new objects (simulating fresh data from API).
4. Without `trackBy`, observe that all DOM elements are re‑created (you can check by adding a timestamp to each item).
5. Add a `trackBy` function that returns `item.id`.
6. Verify that items that didn't change keep their DOM state (timestamps remain the same).
hints: Implement `trackById(index: number, item: any): number { return item.id; }`.
Use `(click)="refresh()"` that does `this.items = this.items.map(i => ({...i, timestamp: Date.now()}))` but keep same ids.
Observe that without trackBy, timestamps all update; with trackBy, they stay the same for unchanged ids.
expectedOutput: With trackBy, only the updated items' timestamps change; other DOM elements are reused.
